title: Timeboxed launch experiment grid and metrics journal
executive_summary: One-page timeboxed experiment grid to validate key launch assumptions for the upcoming beta. Purpose: reduce blast radius by running short (1–2 week) experiments that exercise traffic shaping, fallback routing, and cost-control knobs while tracking a compact KPI set. This doc is a living journal: record outcomes, quick wins, and stop/continue decisions.
experiment_grid:
Format: row per experiment, columns = hypothesis / success metric (primary) / safety criteria / owner / duration (days) / rollout window / quick-fail trigger. Example entries:
- EXP-01: Canary model variant for low-latency tier / primary metric = p95 latency delta <= +30ms at 50% traffic / safety = error-rate < 1% absolute increase / owner = Marcus / duration = 7 / window = 10:00–16:00 PT / quick-fail = sustained error-rate > 1.5% for 5 min.
- EXP-02: KV-prefix cache warmup policy / primary = median token cost reduction >= 8% for chat workload / safety = user-facing correctness regression <= 0.5% per prompt sample / owner = Asha / duration = 14 / window = off-peak / quick-fail = correctness regressions flagged by eval harness.
Notes: keep experiments orthogonal; prefer one independent variable per experiment. Use feature flags and traffic caps. Capture exact config used (model version, quantization profile, batch size, routing policy) in the experiment comment line.
kpi_sheet:
Core KPI set (compact, per-experiment):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms)
- Cost: tokens per request USD (estimated) and aggregate spend delta vs baseline
- Quality: prompt-level pass rate on golden prompt set (binary pass/fail) and BLEU-like similarity for structured outputs
- Reliability: request error rate (4xx/5xx) and SLO burn minutes per day
- User impact: % of blocked/sampled sessions experiencing fallback response
- Operational: alerts triggered, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to resolve (MTTR)
Logging conventions: include the baseline snapshot id (e.g., baseline-2026-02-01-v3) and timestamp. Record pre/post daily rollup in the journal section.
roadmap_milestones:
Timebox plan (high level):
- Week 0: Prep templates, golden prompt set, infra gating checklist, and smoke tests. Owners: Asha + SRE.
- Week 1: Run EXP-01 (canary variant) at 5% traffic -> expand to 20% if safety ok. Deliverable: latency & error delta report.
- Week 2: Run EXP-02 (cache warmup) in isolated tenant -> measure cost delta and correctness. Deliverable: cost model update.
- Week 3: Run EXP-03 (batching policy change) with synthetic load -> measure throughput and tail latency.
- Week 4: Consolidation: cross-experiment retrospective, decide on roll forward, rollback, or iterate.
Dependencies: Dedicated pool capacity booking (infra ticket #IR-2331), rollout flagwork in platform repo, updated monitoring dashboard cards (observability/monitor-44).
readiness_checklist:
Preflight checklist (must pass before user-facing ramp):
- [ ] Infra: Dedicated GPU pool reserved and validated with perf-test harness (ticket IR-2331).
- [ ] Feature flags: kill-switch, traffic cap, and gradual ramp implemented and smoke-tested.
- [ ] Monitoring: KPI cards (latency, cost, error) deployed with alert thresholds and notebooks pinned.
- [ ] Eval: golden prompt suite run against new config with >= 98% pass rate.
- [ ] Rollback plan: explicit model pin + traffic re-route playbook authored and verified in dry-run.
- [ ] Communication: Slack channel created, on-call rota set for the experiment window, and customer success notified for beta cohort.
- [ ] Legal & Privacy: no new data egress; KMS keys validated.
Quick-ops runbook snippets: how to cut traffic to baseline variant (CLI command + console path), how to escalate to SRE, how to run immediate golden prompt re-eval.
decision_criteria_and_risks: Decision rules: run for full timebox unless quick-fail triggers hit. Pass = primary metric improvement or neutral effect with >5% cost savings OR quality impact within tolerance. Fail = primary metric regression beyond safety thresholds or any user-visible correctness regression. Key risks: quiet regressions in niche prompt buckets, telemetry blind spots for low-frequency routes, and billing spikes from misconfigured batching. Mitigations: add sampling for low-frequency routes and run synthetic load bounded by cost cap.
unresolved_questions:
- What is the absolute cost cap per experiment? (finance needs to confirm a hard ceiling)
- Which customers are permitted to be in the live beta if we expand beyond internal tenants? (legal/CS approval)
- Can we automate golden prompt re-eval post-deploy and gate on that?
- Do we have an agreed naming convention for experiment snapshots (tags used in rollout)?
notes_to_self:
- Keep the journal short: one TL;DR line per day and one notable metric graph snapshot.
- When an experiment 'wins' capture the exact commit and config so we can reproduce later.
- Lean on the solutions-eng playbook for customer-facing rollback comms; stamp them before any public expansion.
- Prioritize orthogonality: avoid changing model + batching in same experiment.
- After week 4 retro, convert successful experiments into product tickets with owners for full rollout.
recent_entries:
2026-02-19: EXP-01 dry-run in staging (5m sustained): p95 +12ms, no error spike. Action: proceed to 5% traffic canary.
2026-02-25: EXP-01 live @5% for 24h: p95 +18ms, errors +0.2% absolute (within safety); alerted on anomaly but MTTR = 9m. Decision: expand to 20% next window.
2026-03-05: EXP-02 configured in isolated tenant; golden prompt pass rate = 97.4% (just under target). Action: iterate cache warmup timing and re-run (owner Asha).
final_notes: This doc is intentionally compact and experimental. After the canonical retro, move final state and 'worked' configs to the product-ops canonical repo under /playbooks/launch-experiments and add a minimal runbook to the Console playbook library.
formatting_guidance: Prefer short bullet entries, timestamp each journal line, link to dashboard screenshots (obs cards) and attach perf logs. Use the linked_artifacts list to reference tickets; update that list as new artifacts are created.
